title: Retry Send
statement: Implement `solve(attempts)`. `attempts` is a list of `ok` or `conn` in the order the sender would fail. Retry only `conn`, up to 3 attempts. Return the first `ok`, or `conn` if all consumed attempts were `conn`, or `error` if a non-conn failure appears... The only failure tag is `conn`. Stop at `ok`. If you consume 3 `conn` values without an ok, return `conn`. If the list ends earlier on `conn`, return `conn`. A first `ok` returns `ok`.
hints: Look at most at the first 3 attempts.
Return ok on the first ok.
If you never see ok, return conn.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A retry wrapper around a sender is a decorator object, not an edit of the sender.

editorial: A retry wrapper around a sender is a decorator object, not an edit of the sender. It retries one failure class. A validation error would not be in this list. The cap of 3 stops a dead host from pinning the request. The returned tag is what the caller observes.
